 2026 Sacheon Airshow Concludes... 243,000 Attend Despite Flight Performances Canceled Due to Rain
 by Choi Sungkyung 
 Published 25 Oct.2026 16:32(KST) 
 Share 
 Language 
 Text Size 
 Print 
 Held Oct. 22-25 at Sacheon Airfield and nearby areas... All flight performances canceled on the final two days
Attendance down about 50% from 2024... Safety measures taken amid bad weather
More than 100 domestic and international companies participated... Aerospace and defense exhibitions and industry networking held
 The 2026 Sacheon Airshow concluded its four-day schedule after rain over the final two days of the event led to the cancellation of major flight performances.
 A total of 243,000 visitors attended this year's event, which featured aerospace and defense industry exhibitions, business networking, and educational and hands-on programs.
 According to Sacheon City in South Gyeongsang Province, the 2026 Sacheon Airshow was held from October 22 to 25 at Sacheon Airfield and across the city.
 [Photo provided by Sacheon City] The Air Force Black Eagles aerobatic team performs an aerial display at the 2026 Sacheon Airshow.
 View original image 
 This year's event was scheduled to feature various aviation programs, including a celebratory flight by the Black Eagles and a demonstration flight by the KF-21. However, rain on October 24 and 25, the final two days of the event, led to the cancellation of the flight performances.
 The Sacheon Airshow Organizing Committee decided not to hold the Black Eagles performance, aircraft demonstration flights, or aerobatic displays scheduled for those days, citing weather conditions and visitor safety.
 By contrast, the scheduled flight performances went ahead as planned on October 22, the opening day, and October 23.
 Visitor numbers were recorded at 80,000 on October 22, 100,000 on October 23, 33,000 on October 24, and 30,000 on October 25.
 Total attendance over the four days was 243,000, down about 50% from the 2024 event. The city believes the cancellation of flight performances during the latter part of the event contributed to the decline in attendance.
 In particular, after both the morning and afternoon celebratory flights scheduled for October 25 were canceled, the eight Black Eagles aircraft returned one after another starting at 2:25 p.m., with the return taking about 10 minutes.
 Sacheon Mayor Park Dong-sik and visitors at the event waved to the returning aircraft to bid farewell to the pilots.
 Despite the cancellation of the flight performances, aerospace and defense industry exhibitions and educational and hands-on programs proceeded as conditions allowed.
 This year's Sacheon Airshow was notable for integrating the Aerospace and Defense Industry Exhibition with the existing aviation festival, linking the festival with the industry exhibition.
 More than 100 domestic and international companies took part in the industry exhibition. Two exhibition halls covering 6,050 square meters and an 850-square-meter export consultation center were set up.
 Participating companies showcased aerospace and defense technologies and products in the exhibition area and discussed opportunities for cooperation through export consultations and business programs.
 The event also featured aircraft and weapons and equipment displays on the ground, along with various programs such as aviation simulators and augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) experiences.
 These programs were designed to give members of the public, young people, and families interested in the aviation industry the opportunity to see and experience related technologies and equipment firsthand.
 Sacheon City plans to assess the event's operations and consider ways to improve measures for running programs during bad weather, the industry exhibition, and public participation programs.
 In particular, the city plans to expand networking among companies in the aerospace and defense sectors and improve educational and hands-on programs open to general visitors.
 Photo courtesy of Sacheon City: The Air Force's aerobatic team, the Black Eagles, performs an aerial display at the 2026 Sacheon Airshow.
 View original image 
 Sacheon Mayor Park Dong-sik said, "It is regrettable that flight performances were canceled for two days and visitor numbers fell, but we prioritized visitor safety in running the event. The industry exhibition, business networking, and educational and hands-on programs provided an opportunity to showcase the aerospace and defense industries."
 He added, "We will review the operational experience and areas for improvement identified at this event and work to develop the Sacheon Airshow's role in industry networking and its public participation programs."
 This year's Sacheon Airshow saw a sharp decline in visitor numbers after bad weather led to the cancellation of major flight performances, but the aerospace and defense industry exhibitions and business networking continued.
